title: Poland's ePUAP e-government platform restricted after cyberattack; full operation restored 19 November, COI says
date_note: Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski posted about the attack on a Tuesday evening (money.pl/PAP, 12 November; taken as 10 November, the date COI gives for the restriction); COI says full operation returned on 19 November (Sekurak, 21 November).
geo_basis: national agency headquarters (Ministry of Digital Affairs / COI), city not stated in the sources
summary: Poland’s COI told Sekurak it preventively restricted access to part of the ePUAP system from 10 November, that the attack was detected and stopped, and that full operation returned on 19 November. Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski said the attack came from abroad and that logs showed preparatory activity for a December operation against public administration. COI says the ABW is investigating and it found no sign of spread.
plain: Poland's national online platform for government services was restricted for several days after a cyberattack. The government says the attack was stopped and the platform is fully working again.
exec: Poland’s national citizen-services portal was partly restricted from 10 to 19 November; the Deputy PM says a wider attack on administration was planned for December.
impact: COI says access was preventively restricted from 10 November and services were restored in stages, with full operation on 19 November.

validation.note: Sekurak (quoting COI's written answers) and money.pl/PAP (quoting Gawkowski) each state that an attack on ePUAP was stopped. No page from the ministry or COI itself was read.

review.note: Checked Sekurak and money.pl/PAP: COI restricted part of system (not whole, about 9 days), most services back 15-16 Nov; December plan is Gawkowski's statement; removed unsourced action advice; 19 Nov restoration, ABW, no-spread match COI
